components.description: One semester of release from teaching and administrative duties at full pay for a faculty member who will spend the majority of academic time caring for a newborn or newly placed child; thesis advising and research continue. Taken in any term within one year of the child's arrival.

components.institution_label: Leaves Provided Under the Family and Medical Leave Act
components.description: Federal FMLA: up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period for the employee's own serious health condition (including pregnancy and childbirth), the birth and care of a newborn, adoption or foster placement, or care of a seriously ill child, parent or spouse. Restated for faculty in P&P 7.5.2 (the 12-week personal-leave entitlement) and detailed in PPM 4.5.
components.faculty_group_note: eligible faculty members (P&P 7.5.2); regular full-time or part-time employees working 50% or more (PPM 4.5)
components.eligible_parent_wording: an employee's own serious health condition (including conditions related to pregnancy and childbirth); the birth and care of the employee's newborn child; the placement of a child with the employee for adoption or foster care
components.duration_note: Statute: 'a total of 12 workweeks'; MIT texts say 'up to 12 weeks in a 12-month period' (rolling 12-month period measured backward). Unpaid leave beyond 12 weeks is personal leave (mit_c8).
components.service_requirement: 12 months and 1,250 hours (29 U.S.C. 2611(2)); MIT: employed at least one year and working 50% or more of a normal work week
components.dual_employee_rule: spouses both employed by MIT: combined total of 12 weeks within a 12-month period for care of a newborn or newly placed child
components.medical_certification_note: health care provider certification for the employee's own serious health condition or care of a seriously ill family member
components.time_window: leave must be completed within 12 months of the date of birth (or placement)
components.notice: as much advance notice as possible; at least two weeks preferred (PPM 4.5.5); at least two weeks for parental leave (P&P 7.5.6.2)

Rules file V1's example cites an 'MIT childbirth leave 8 weeks at 100%'. No saved source states a childbirth-specific period, length or pay level (PPM 4.3.5, which may hold it, is not saved), so the childbirth disability is coded as the generic sick plan (mit_c4, mit_c5). If PPM 4.3.5 (in force 2018-02-27) were saved and covers faculty, it would likely be coded employer_childbirth_benefit under V1/V1b.

Not components: sabbatical and Junior Faculty Research Leave (research purposes, cannot be used for a birth), professional leave (professional development or public service), domestic violence leave (7.5.7), 'release arrangements offered by Schools' (no terms saved).

U8: the member is a tenure-track faculty member with two years of service, eligible for FMLA. The teaching relief (mit_c1) carries a majority-caregiver condition (R6, gender-neutral). PPM 4.5.1/4.5.2's 'combination of the medical leave period and the additional period for child care leave should not exceed 12 weeks' is FMLA's own 12 weeks (mit_c2 covers both purposes), so no leave_limits entry is recorded.

Birth parent chain: FMLA 12 workweeks (mit_c2) from the birth, with the Massachusetts Parental Leave Act 8 weeks (mit_c3), sick pay (mit_c4, no length; mit_c5 extended illness up to 6 months, discretionary) concurrent with it, and family sick time (mit_c6) and own balances (mit_c7) within it → personal leave beyond 12 weeks (mit_c8, general, discretionary, not counted); teaching relief one semester at full pay (mit_c1), in any term within a year of the birth, not linked (the window places nothing).

Non-birth parent chain: FMLA 12 workweeks (mit_c2) with the Massachusetts Parental Leave Act 8 weeks (mit_c3) concurrent, family sick time 40 hours (mit_c6) and own balances (mit_c7) within it → personal leave beyond 12 weeks (mit_c8, not counted); teaching relief one semester at full pay (mit_c1, majority-caregiver condition), not linked.
